correctness.rationale: Faces of X_n are exactly the words in {0,+,-}^n with adjacent nonzero orientations agreeing; reversing path vertices reverses word order AND arc orientation. A fixed simplex has 2p arcs in reflection pairs and orientation sign (-1)^p. For m=floor((n-1)/2), central constraints yield a bijection of fixed faces with those of X_m. In the augmented Hopf trace, each fixed face contributes -(-1)^p, so the reduced Lefschetz trace is χ̃(X_m). The established homotopy X_n≃S^m (Caputi–Collari–Smith, Prop.2.2) then forces sign (-1)^(m+floor((m-1)/2)), with m=0 handled using χ̃(X_0)=-1. The displayed mod-eight pattern follows by exact parity; the quotient over Q is the invariant eigenspace after barycentric subdivision and averaging. Independently enumerated fixed words and supertraces for n=1..11 and read original check.py, but the all-n argument is the fixed-face proof plus cited sphere theorem.
residual_risks: Relies on the correct prior nonequivariant sphere theorem; does not classify the integral quotient or fixed-point topology.

value.rationale: A discrete symmetry action on the uniquely nonzero homology of a canonical infinite graph-complex family is an intrinsic equivariant invariant not fixed by its known sphere homotopy type. The exact eight-residue classification resolves which sphere orientation survives the quotient and distinguishes even cases where previously known joins are insufficient. This is a focused structural theorem rather than a renamed nonequivariant sphere count.
residual_risks: The method is an elementary Hopf-trace application once the correct face involution and known homotopy theorem are in place; no stronger equivariant homotopy statement follows.

final_claim: For every n>=1 the unique integral reduced homology group of the bidirected-path multipath complex X_n is Z in degree floor((n-1)/2); reversal acts by -1 for n mod 8 in {1,2,3,4}, by +1 for {0,5,6,7}. The rational quotient homology is the invariant line exactly in the plus-sign residues.
limitations: Relies on the published nonequivariant sphere theorem.
Finite trace checks n<=11 independently corroborate only small cases.
The character is integral on a Z-line; quotient homology is asserted only rationally, not integrally.
An unindexed earlier calculation of the exact path-reversal character or an equivalent equivariant discrete-Morse matching may exist.
The stronger equivariant homotopy type and integral orbit-space homology were not established.
